title: Cloud Listing Launch: Mini Playbook & Snippet Workbench
summary: Lightweight operational checklist + copy snippet bank to accelerate partner marketplace launches. Prioritizes a minimum viable tile, short elevator copy, and a telemetry + compliance acceptance slice for beta partners.
content:
Purpose:
- Fast, repeatable checklist for getting a partner/product tile from intake -> published in a cloud marketplace (AWS/GCP/Azure).
- Provide a ‘snippet workbench’: short copy variants, 1-line elevator, 2 tile length versions, and basic FAQ + billing notes to A/B quickly.

Intended audience:
- PMs running partner listings, partner SEs, partner marketing, and listing engineers.

Open questions / assumptions (notes to self):
- Q: Does the partner always provide a logo with transparent background? If not, we need an asset remediation step.
- Q: For private deployment product entries, do we need an extra KMS box callout? Ask security (Lena).
- We assume SKU mapping will be handled by billing ops; include mapping template but not final mappings.

Minimum Acceptance Gates (beta / fast path):
1) Legal & Compliance: partner signed NDA + minimal data flow diagram attached (PDF).
2) Security: transient architecture diagram showing where customer data resides + KMS note for private deployments.
3) Technical: integration smoke test (hello-world flow) pass link to GH action + sample request/response.
4) Marketing copy: one long description (<=250 words), one short description (<=60 words), 1-line elevator, 2 tile-length headlines.
5) Assets: logo PNG 1024px square, 16:9 hero image (1920x1080) or acceptable placeholder, optional product video link.
6) Billing & SKU: placeholder SKU with pricing tier table (dev/prod) + free trial flag.
7) Telemetry hooks: event names for new trial, trial-to-paid conversion, and API errors.
8) Publish checklist: PR to marketplace repo + acceptance owner signed off.

Snippet Workbench (copy variants) - use as quick swap bank:
- 1-line elevator (primary): "Enterprise-ready LLM inference: predictable latency, lower unit costs, and flexible deployment models."
- 1-line elevator (alt): "Run LLMs reliably at scale — hosted, dedicated, or in your VPC."

- Short description (<=60 words):
  "Redwood Inference delivers production-grade LLM inference with transparent performance and cost controls. Deploy via hosted API, reserved dedicated capacity, or private VPC for regulated workloads. Start with a free trial and scale with SLA-backed capacity."

- Long description (<=250 words):
  "Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running large language models in production. Our unified runtime optimizes latency and cost through intelligent batching, KV caching, and quantization knobs while providing model versioning, rollout controls, and observability. Choose hosted API for fast integration, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for sensitive workloads. Built-in telemetry, traceability, and rollback policies reduce launch risk and make scaling straightforward. Ideal for product teams shipping chat, generation, and embedding features with strict SLOs."

- Tile headline options (short):
  1) "Predictable LLM inference — hosted, dedicated, private"
  2) "Low-cost, reliable LLM serving for production apps"

- CTA variants:
  - "Try free — 14-day credits"
  - "Request a demo & SLA"
  - "Get started: quickstart + SDK"

SKU & Pricing Template (fast-fill):
- SKU ID (placeholder): RWINF-MKT-BETA-001
- Tier names: starter | standard | dedicated
- Billing units: token-generation (per 1k tokens) + embedding-unit (per 1k vectors) + reserved-gpu-hour for Dedicated
- Trial: 14 days, $Credits: 200 USD equivalent

Technical Acceptance Snippets (to paste into listing docs):
- "Supported APIs: text-generation, chat, embeddings, reranking. SDKs for Python, Node. Streaming responses available for interactive flows."
- "All hosted data is isolated per-tenant and retained per customer-configured retention policies; Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM."

Telemetry & SLA hooks (operational):
- Events to emit: marketplace_trial_started, marketplace_trial_converted, marketplace_api_error, marketplace_quota_limit_hit
- Minimal SLO claims: 99.5% uptime for published tiles; response-time buckets to be documented per SKU.

Acceptance workflow (step-by-step):
1) Intake form -> PM assigns owner (Owen).
2) Asset collection -> marketing validates hero/logo (Diego).
3) Security review -> attach architecture.pdf (Lena).
4) Tech smoke -> link GH action or GCP/AWS test and confirm sample payload returns expected schema.
5) Copy + pricing -> finalize snippets and SKU table.
6) PR -> marketplace repo -> integration test run.
7) Sign-off -> go-live on staging -> monitor telemetry for 72 hours -> promote to public.

Rollout notes & rollback criteria (quick):
- Canary publish: 10% of search impressions -> monitor 3 metrics: conversion trial-start rate, API error rate, latency percentiles (p50/p95).
- Auto-rollback triggers: trial-start drop >30% vs baseline OR error rate spike >2x baseline OR p95 latency >2x target for >15 minutes.

Copy hygiene checklist (QA):
- No vendor-brand conflicts in short copy.
- Avoid absolute promises (e.g., "always", "never").
- Confirm legal-approved phrasing for data residency and compliance.

Notes to shipping PM / next steps:
- Add KMS callout checkbox for private deploy entries.
- Create a small Airtable template for collected assets + status column for each acceptance gate.
- Run a dry publish with internal-only flag to validate asset rendering across AWS/GCP tiles (Owen to schedule).

Slack links / references:
- Related convo: #marketplace-launches @channel thread on 2026-01-08 (see pinned message).
- Security question thread: slack.com/archives/SECU-9876 (ask Lena Kaur for final wording).

Final owner & reviewers:
- Owner: Asha Patel (go-to-market)
- Reviewers: Diego Ramos (marketing), Lena Kaur (security), Owen McBride (engineering).

Appendix: quick paste templates
- Wireframe alt text: "Hero: screenshot of console showing model selection + latency bar"
- Example sample payload (for tech doc):
  {"input": "Hello, world", "model": "rw-inference-v1"}

-- end of mini playbook --
